correctness.rationale: By the published Type-A characterization, two binary length-n words have two distinct common one-deletion descendants precisely when they are complementary alternating phases on their unique first-to-last mismatch interval of length>=2. Therefore neighbors of x biject with alternating intervals in x. Maximal 1-runs of the difference string have lengths h_i, contributing binom(h_i+1,2) each. Unique run decomposition yields F(z,u)=2(1+R)/(1-z-zR), R=sum_{h>=1}z^h*u^binom(h+1,2); differentiation at u=1 yields exactly mean n-2+2^(1-n) and variance 6n-30+(2n^2+6n+17)/2^(n-1)-4^(1-n), and limiting degree/n->1 in probability. n=1 has two zero-degree vertices. Independent direct distinct-deletion-ball adjacency over all binary words n=1..8 matched every predicted degree and histogram. The all-n conclusion uses the Type-A theorem and formal combinatorics, not finite tests.
